title: Professional email: set up, write well, stay organised

say: Your address is the first thing a stranger sees. A nickname may be fun among friends, but an employer may not take it seriously.

panel.heading: Choose a professional address

say: Use your real name in a simple pattern. If it is taken, add a middle initial, your trade or your town, not random numbers.

panel.heading: Choose a professional address

say: Tap Compose. The To box is for the people who must read and act.

panel.heading: Know every box before you send
items: To: the people who must act
Cc: people kept informed; everyone sees them
Bcc: hidden addresses, to protect privacy
Subject: what the email is about
Attachment: up to 25 MB, or send a Drive link

say: Cc, carbon copy, keeps people informed. Everyone can see who was copied.

say: Step one. A specific subject of 4 to 9 words, like Please approve venue payment by Friday 5 pm. Never leave it empty.

panel.heading: Write an email that gets a reply
items: Specific subject: topic, action, date
Greeting that fits the reader
Request in the first two lines
Short details and a real deadline
Polite close, your name, then read aloud

say: Step two. Fit the greeting to the reader. Dear Mrs Okafor for a senior person or stranger, Hello Mr Musa for someone you know.

say: Step three. Put your request in the first two lines. This is called Bottom Line Up Front, so the question is not hidden at the end.

say: Step four. Short details, and a real deadline with day and time, not ASAP.

say: Step five. Close politely and read it aloud. Please and could you turn an order into a request. No capital-letter shouting, no text-speak like pls.

Files renamed clearly, sent as PDF

panel.heading: Keep your inbox under control

cards.d: Labels work like folders, but one email can carry two labels. Star what you must reply to this week.
Archive finished emails. They stay in All Mail, and search such as from: or has:attachment finds them.
Report spam to train the filter. Never click links in emails that promise prizes or ask for your BVN.

say: Archive finished emails. They are never lost, and search finds them. Try from: and a name, or has:attachment.

say: Report spam to train the filter. Emails promising prizes or asking for your BVN are usually scams. Never click their links.

say: Use a strong password of at least 8 characters and write it somewhere safe at home, not in your phone notes. Add your phone number for recovery.
Google, your bank and WODDI will never ask for your password or the 6-digit code. Anyone who asks is trying to take over your account.

panel.heading: Protect your account
items: Strong password of at least 8 characters
Password written somewhere safe at home
Phone number added for recovery
Never share your password or the 6-digit code

say: To remember. Use your real name. To acts, Cc is informed, Bcc hides. Put the request first under a specific subject.
Rename files, prefer PDF, and mention attachments. Keep the inbox tidy, and follow up in the same thread after about 3 working days.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Use your real name in your email address
To acts, Cc is informed, Bcc hides addresses
Specific subject, request in the first two lines
Rename files, prefer PDF, mention attachments
Label, star and archive; report spam
